title: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Certification Framework
summary: This thread covers the formalization of the AEO program, evolving from a basic application process to a structured regulatory framework involving renewal, audit, and suspension protocols.

evolution.structure: Transitioned from a static recognition status to a dynamic, time-bound certification requiring periodic renewal and audit.
evolution.governance: Introduced formal risk-based monitoring and automated notification systems for status changes.

timeline.change: Established risk management and suspension/cancellation protocols for AEO status.
Defined specific timelines for renewal, audit, and formal notification of status changes.

Authorized Economic Operator: Consignments belonging to an authorized entity may still be subject to physical examination or inspection by customs officials if credible intelligence information is received.
The certification held by an institution does not preclude customs authorities from performing standard assessment or inspection duties when specific intelligence warrants such action.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is empowered to conduct physical examination, inspection, or assessment of goods belonging to certified institutions based on credible intelligence reports.
Customs Clearance: This process, including physical inspection and assessment, remains applicable to certified entities whenever credible intelligence suggests the need for such intervention.

Authorized Economic Operator: The Center is mandated to immediately notify all relevant customs offices regarding the suspension, cancellation, or downgrading of an authorized economic operator's certification.
Notification procedures must follow the specific operational template defined in the relevant appendix of the standing order.
National Board of Revenue: The Customs Automation Branch of the Board is a primary recipient of information regarding the status of entity certifications to ensure system-wide coordination.
Customs Risk Management: The Customs Risk Management Commissionerate must be immediately updated whenever an entity's status is revoked or downgraded to maintain accurate risk profiles.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The Systems Manager is responsible for updating the customs automation infrastructure based on notifications regarding changes to operator status.

Authorized Economic Operator: The Authorized Economic Operator Center allows for an extension of the time limit for existing certified entities to fulfill applicable operational conditions.

The maximum duration for this extension is set to a specific period, and failure to comply with the required conditions within this timeframe will result in the suspension or cancellation of the entity's certification.

This authority is responsible for issuing official extensions regarding the fulfillment of conditions for recognized Authorized Economic Operators and holds the power to suspend or revoke certifications upon non-compliance.
Authorized Economic Operator (Recognitio: Rule 20(3) of these rules provides the legal framework under which the Authorized Economic Operator Center may grant extensions for meeting certification requirements.

member_objects.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) সনদ এর মেয়াদ, নবায়ন ও পরিবর্তন

Authorized Economic Operator: The recognition certificate for an Authorized Economic Operator is valid for a period of one year.
An Authorized Economic Operator must maintain the mandatory standards and criteria required for the certification at all times.
The certification or benefits provided to an Authorized Economic Operator may be temporarily suspended if the renewal application is not submitted within the specified timeframe.

An Authorized Economic Operator is required to report any identified customs-related errors to the designated center and relevant customs station immediately, though self-reported errors will not negatively impact the certification status unless they involve serious offences like duty evasion or smuggling.
Upon identifying a customs error, an Authorized Economic Operator must investigate the root cause and implement preventative measures to ensure it does not recur.

The Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Center is responsible for receiving renewal applications, which must be submitted within a specific number of days following the expiry of the current certification.
The center must conduct verification and onsite post-clearance audits within a defined period upon receiving a complete renewal application to process the certification renewal.
Entities must report significant business changes, such as legal status, address, business nature, or management structure, to the center using the prescribed format.

The center must be notified within a specific time period if there is a change in the legal entity of the Authorized Economic Operator, at which point the center may cancel the old certificate and issue a new one if all legal requirements are met.
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: The Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Center is required to provide updated information regarding all renewals to the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Committee by the tenth day of every month.

Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Rules: These rules establish the procedural framework for issuing, suspending, and cancelling Authorized Economic Operator certification.
The rules define the specific conditions under which a certification may be suspended, reviewed, and either permanently cancelled, downgraded, or reinstated by the designated committee.
Authorized Economic Operator: This authority is responsible for issuing official notifications regarding the status of an Authorized Economic Operator, including notices of suspension, cancellation, or reinstatement.
An operator facing suspension must be provided with a show-cause notice and an opportunity to provide a satisfactory explanation for the alleged violations before a final decision is made.
The certification of an operator may be subject to permanent cancellation, downgrading, or reinstatement depending on the findings of the review process.
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: This committee is empowered to review evidence and explanations provided by operators regarding alleged violations and to make final decisions on the status of their certification.
